items.text: I finally revealed my bedroom non-negotiable to the new guy I'm dating... his horrified reaction was worse than I feared: DEAR JANE
items.article: I've been dating someone new for a few weeks. He's everything I could ask for in a man - kind, funny, handsome and we share the same values - and I have fallen completely head over heels. I've been dating someone new for a few weeks. He's everything I could ask for in a man – kind, funny, handsome and we share the same values – and I have fallen completely head over heels. Up until recently our casual dates consisted of grabbing coffee, dinner, drinks or going to the movies. In other words, all very public. But last week, he asked if he could come over with a bottle of wine and cook dinner for me at my place. I knew what coming over implied – and what he would expect after a few glasses of pinot noir – and my heart sank. You see, I'm not the 'wait for marriage' type of girl, but I also don't rush to jump into bed with someone I don't fully know yet. I'd rather wait to be someone's serious girlfriend before sleeping with them – and we have yet to put labels on our relationship. Still, I agreed to let him come over anyways, but was racked with anxiety the entire night about having to possibly reject his advances and come clean about my 'rule.'

items.article: Molly and Taylor Haylett explain the changes to how they managed their finances when they started a family. When Molly and Taylor Haylett started their family, they hadn't really planned for what it would mean financially. "Our first child surprised us, so we weren't prepared for it," says Molly, 30, a financial adviser from Essex. Molly and Taylor, who's a train driver, were earning similar amounts, but once Molly spent more time at home with their baby, the balance changed. "Taylor's career propelled and mine took a step back," she says. "There's an unintended impact on the person who spends more time at home with the kids." One of the things the couple decided to do was have Taylor contribute to Molly's pension while she was off work. "We were looking after both our futures, not just Taylor's," Molly says.

items.article: Economics editor Faisal Islam examines whether the north-west city can be a template for the entire country. Burnham's 'Manchesterism' got him to No 10 - but will it work for the UK? It was just five months ago when Andy Burnham retreated to his mayor's office in Manchester, having been blocked by Labour's ruling executive from standing for parliament. When I met him there a few weeks later, he told me he planned to deal with his disappointment with some ambitious plans for his city region. Burnham told me he wanted to appeal directly to Fifa to host the final of the women's football World Cup in 2035 Manchester instead of Wembley. "Imagine how electrifying that is for any girl growing up in the north of England," he said. He said he was also joining forces with other mayors for a "Great Northern" Olympic bid across the north of England, and a plan was also afoot to host the Ryder Cup in Bolton. Sports bodies needed "re-educating" about the rest of the country, he said. Manchester has already poached the Brit Awards from London after half a century in the capital.

items.text: I got a first look at Apple’s new £2k iPhone – it’s not just the price that makes it stand out
items.article: After years of holding out, Apple has learnt from its rivals with its first folding model, the iPhone Duo. These are my first impressions The products or services listed have been independently tested by our journalists. We earn a commission from the affiliate links in this article. Read more > Apple has entered the foldable phone race with the iPhone Duo, following years of speculation about whether the company would ever bend its famously rigid design philosophy. Barely a month after Samsung dropped its latest Galaxy Z Fold 8 , this is the moment Apple stakes its claim in a category it has avoided for the last decade. I was at the launch event at Apple’s HQ in Cupertino, California for a first look. Similar in size to a British passport, the new smartphone unfolds like a miniature book to reveal a large 7.6-inch inner screen. When closed, it’s shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, and when opened, it resembles a small iPad. What makes the iPhone Duo worth your attention isn’t just that it’s the first hinged phone with an Apple logo, but that it addresses some of the biggest frustrations currently plaguing folding mobiles. You can barely see the crease on the inner display, and it doesn’t look like a cheap plastic sheet. It’s intuitive to use, and fully waterproof, which is rare among rivals. Whether all that justifies a £2,000 price tag, however, is another question entirely.

items.article: Georgina Le Grice is no stranger to horror stories, but she never expected to find herself in one when her family's picturesque 18th-century property was falling apart, and there was no money to save it. Georgina Le Grice is no stranger to horror stories, thanks to her job as a London-based literary agent. But she never expected to find herself in one, at her family’s Cornish mansion, Trereife House. The picturesque 18th-century property was falling apart, and there was no money to save it. ‘I moved into Trereife House when I was just two,’ says Georgina, 24, ‘and my elderly grandmother moved out. It had 80 acres of land, 14 rooms and six enormous, ornate bedrooms. We never had heating, and I went to bed in winter in layers of clothes and with two duvets. But I didn’t mind, because I loved the house.’ From a young age, Georgina knew she and her younger brother Peter, 23, were heirs to an estate with a remarkable history. The house has been home to the Le Grice family since 1798. Saviour: Ruth Watson at Trereife House in Penzance with Tim, Peter, Georgina and Elizabeth Le Grice But generation after generation was hit by crippling death duties and running costs. We used sampling swabs to gather up any bacteria that might have been growing on the handles of the most popular bikes: Forest, Lime, Voi, and the classic Santander Bike, also known as the Boris Bike.

items.article: Martin Seligman reveals how with positive thinking, determination and self-will you can achieving almost anything. Published: 17:30, 17 September 2026 | Updated: 17:30, 17 September 2026 As usual, Shakespeare got it right. ‘All things be ready, if our minds be so,’ says King Harry in Henry V: when the English are vastly outnumbered by the French forces, he has no doubt what will bring about an English victory on St Crispin’s Day. Sheer will , he tells the assembled Lords. Will is at the root of agency; willpower drives performance and success. Even in these depressed and depressing times, that seems self-evident. But over 50 years ago, the world-famous psychologist, Martin Seligman, witnessed the collapse of will in his best student at Cornell University. Faced with a project well within her capabilities she simply gave up, because she had convinced herself she couldn’t do it. Her professor realised that, ‘in 1968, psychology had no vocabulary for what I wanted to say’.

items.article: A construction worker says he had a three-hour conversation with Jesus and vividly remembers his face in an experience that changed the course of his life. By CHRIS MELORE, US DEPUTY SCIENCE EDITOR Published: 16:00, 12 September 2026 | Updated: 05:54, 13 September 2026 A construction worker in Tennessee says he came face-to-face with Jesus when he nearly died and is now sharing exactly what he looked like. Mike McKinsey was a superintendent in 2004 when he suffered a ruptured appendix that nearly killed him and required emergency surgery due to the severe infection. As his life hung in the balance, McKinsey claimed that Jesus walked into the operating room in physical form and took his hand, transporting the dying man to a hill overlooking what he perceived as heaven. Unlike other depictions across Christianity, McKinsey said he vividly remembered Jesus having darker skin, green or blue-green eyes and shoulder-length, wavy brown hair.

items.text: New 'code' found in Egypt's Great Pyramid may finally reveal its true purpose
items.article: The Great Pyramid has guarded its secrets behind millions of tons of stone, but a new paper claims its greatest message may have been hiding in plain sight. By STACY LIBERATORE, US SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY EDITOR Published: 20:45, 10 September 2026 | Updated: 19:33, 11 September 2026 Independent researcher Sefy Levy argued that carefully chosen measurements on the monument’s exterior form a numerical system designed to survive long after its builders were gone. Rather than being carved into a wall , the alleged code is said to be embedded in the pyramid’s height, base, sloping sides and overall shape. Levy claimed those dimensions produce striking matches with the cycles of the moon, the calendar and planets visible to the naked eye. He believes the numbers were intended to preserve the Egyptians’ knowledge of mathematics, time and the heavens for eternity.

But even the most ardent fans of the meat may be put off by a recent report, which found that just two rashers of the least healthy products on sale in supermarkets contained more than 40 per cent of an adult’s daily salt limit. Their findings will come as a relief to fans of Morrisons ' Nitrate Free Unsmoked Back Bacon, which was named the healthiest option. However, it's bad news if your go-to is the Finnebrogue Naked Unsmoked Streaky Bacon or Morrisons' The Best Extra Thick Cut Unsmoked Back Bacon, which were found to contain the most saturated fat and salt, respectively.

items.article: In a viral clip, posted by the New Zealand-based podcast The Morning Shift, you can hear a strange repetitive sound being played. However, no one has been able to agree on what the message says. By WILIAM HUNTER, SENIOR SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY REPORTER Published: 14:46, 10 September 2026 | Updated: 16:15, 10 September 2026 The internet has been left bitterly divided over a strange audio illusion. In a viral clip, posted by the New Zealand–based podcast The Morning Shift, you can hear a strange repetitive sound being played. However, no one has been able to agree on what the message is saying. Some social media users are certain that they can hear the phrase 'no way, no way, no way', while others swear to hear 'well, well, well'.
